Bleeding-edge hardware is going to have the least amount of driver support, meaning you'll have the most problems with it, especially as you'll be introducing another layer of complexity by compiling the drivers on a non-Linux system. Go with last-gen graphics, or even the generation before that -- they're plenty powerful enough to drive high-end monitors for "scrolling," and they'll give you far less grief in the driver support department.

Currently, the UK buys a lot of cheap steel from China. China is also a big export market for British steel, but import tariffs have risen significantly over recent years, with talks of it rising to around 46% in the future. The EU was on the brink of imposing tariffs for Chinese steel being sold to EU countries, which would have been a big boost to the British steel industry, but we are not a member of the EU anymore, so it no longer applies to us. In 2003, President Bush introduced import tariffs on British steel being sold to the US, which is one of the reasons we have been doing business with China.

If the US removes the import tariffs completely, Britain will commit to selling the US an extra 200,000 tonnes of high quality steel every year, which is currently going to China. Profits from the steel sold to the US produced in nationalised British steelworks will be put towards boosting steel production in the UK, in order to combat China's steel monopoly.
